title: Tailwind CSS: utilities, configuration and components

videos.script: For twelve lessons the CSS has lived in stylesheets, and the HTML has carried class names that say what a thing is: an event card, a menu. {{flip}} Tailwind turns that round. Its classes say what a thing looks like. Padding four. Text extra large. Rounded corners. A page is styled by stacking those small classes in the HTML, and you hardly write a stylesheet at all. {{reaction}} The first reaction of most people who know CSS is that this is wrong. It looks like inline styles with extra steps. {{why}} It is used on a great many sites anyway, and for reasons worth understanding. Nothing has to be named. Nothing leaks from one component into another. And the values come from a scale, so a page stays consistent. {{same}} Underneath, it is the CSS of this course. Every class is a rule you could have written. The scale is a set of custom properties, like lesson 10's tokens. The breakpoints are lesson 11's media queries. {{tool}} It needs one tool, a command that reads your HTML and writes the stylesheet. This lesson installs it, builds with it, and opens what it wrote. {{close}}
